extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed final mechanism ontology from primary methods/results/figure captions; no unsupported database-only mechanism is promoted.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Allomyrinasin and andricin B against Staphylococcus pseudintermedius MW767056
mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper directly supports bacterial membrane disruption/permeabilization for allomyrinasin and andricin B using bacteriolysis and calcein-leakage assays.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct mechanism evidence is limited to membrane perturbation in S. pseudintermedius; biofilm, serum, and in vivo outcomes are phenotypic efficacy evidence.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Allomyrinasin, andricin B, and pinipesin against S. pseudintermedius, S. cohnii, and M. canis biofilms
mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper supports anti-biofilm phenotype through MBIC/MBEC rows and biofilm formation-rate assays, with Table 2 as the row-level source.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Biofilm rows are not promoted to a direct molecular mechanism beyond the separately supported membrane-disruption assays.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Allomyrinasin and andricin B in the S. pseudintermedius mouse skin infection model
mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper supports in vivo anti-infective and anti-inflammatory phenotype via reduced bacterial load and lower IL-6/TNF-alpha expression in treated skin.
